parts.title: Part 2 · How a module is delivered: design to production

title: Terraform for Enterprise Production
summary: A practical guide to building and running Terraform in enterprise AWS. Part 1 covers the techniques: module structure, safe state, validation, secrets, refactoring, and CI/CD checks. Part 2 puts them into one delivery process for a team codebase: base and composition modules, shared conventions, testing, decision records, and a security gate every module passes before it reaches an environment.
closingBody: I'm happy to go into more detail on any of this: module design trade-offs, moving state safely, testing modules, or running a security gate in CI/CD.

title: Enterprise Cloud Migration: Assess, Mobilize & Modernize
summary: A practical guide to large cloud migrations on AWS: choosing a rapid (4–6 week) or deep (3–4 month) assessment, sizing from real usage, building the 3-year cost case with Savings Plans and Microsoft licensing, designing the landing zone, planning waves, and deciding what to modernize along the way.
closingBody: I'm happy to go into more detail on any of this: scoping an assessment, building the cost model, or planning migration waves.

title: Kubernetes from Zero to Production on Amazon EKS
summary: A path from never having used Kubernetes to running Amazon EKS in production. Part 1 covers the basics on a free local cluster. Part 2 teaches the core concepts: how a cluster works, workloads, networking, storage, access, and packaging. Part 3 moves to Amazon EKS and builds the platform. Part 4 covers the real challenges of operating it: delivery, GitOps, autoscaling, observability, incident triage, and upgrades.
closingBody: I'm happy to go into more detail on any of this: how the pieces fit together, ingress costs, RBAC design, or how I triage incidents.

title: Linux for DevOps: From First Terminal to On-Call Troubleshooting
summary: A hands-on path for new graduates and associate engineers: from your first hour on a Linux server to diagnosing real production faults. Every module ends with a break-fix lab: you break a throwaway VM on purpose, then find and fix the cause with the same tools used on call.
closingBody: I'm happy to go into more detail on any of this: how to practise troubleshooting safely, which fundamentals matter most early on, or how a break-fix lab is put together.

title: My AI Journey: From Copy-Paste to Agentic Workflows
summary: The story of how I brought AI into my work as a Lead DevOps engineer and DevOps architect: a curious ChatGPT question in late 2022, the copy-paste years, then AI as a co-worker, writer, and planner, and finally agentic workflows that deliver platform code compliant by design and apps built for SOC compliance. Every chapter ends with an exercise to try on your own work.
closingQuestion: Where are you on your own AI journey?
closingBody: If you're bringing AI into your own work, or you're stuck at one of these stages, I'd be glad to hear how it's going and compare notes on what's worked.
